approachQuestion.prompt:
Find a ledger value

A rectangular read-only matrix has r rows and c columns, both positive. Each row is strictly increasing, and each row first value exceeds the preceding row last value. Given x, return whether x occurs. 1 <= r*c <= 200000. Random access is constant time. Examples: [[2,5],[8,11]], x=8 -> true; x=6 -> false. Prefer work growing least with the total cell count, then memory.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Binary-search virtual indices 0 through r*c-1, reading index k as matrix[k//c][k%c].
options.feedback: The cross-row ordering makes the virtual row-major array sorted.

options.text: Flatten every cell into a new array, then binary-search that array.
options.feedback: Flattening is correct but copies all input cells before the search. Virtual indexing avoids this work and storage.

options.text: Binary-search only the first row because every later row has larger values.
options.feedback: For [[2,5],[8,11]], x=8 exists outside the first row.

feedback.reason: Binary-search virtual indices 0 through r*c-1, reading index k as matrix[k//c][k%c]. The cross-row ordering makes the virtual row-major array sorted.
details: Binary-search virtual indices 0 through r*c-1, reading index k as matrix[k//c][k%c]. The cross-row ordering makes the virtual row-major array sorted.

Decode virtual index k using the column count. Cross-row ordering is essential: independently sorted rows alone do not make row-major order sorted. Virtual indexing obtains the flattened order without allocating a flattened copy.
“Binary-search virtual indices 0 through r*c-1, reading index k as matrix[k//c][k%c].”: The cross-row ordering makes the virtual row-major array sorted.
“Flatten every cell into a new array, then binary-search that array.”: Flattening is correct but copies all input cells before the search. Virtual indexing avoids this work and storage.
“Binary-search only the first row because every later row has larger values.”: For [[2,5],[8,11]], x=8 exists outside the first row.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Analyze the iterative virtual-index method. Integer multiplication, division, remainder and cell access are constant time; index products fit. No matrix flattening or recursion. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

feedback.reason: Binary search over r*c virtual positions uses constant-time index decoding.
details: The virtual sorted array contains r*c cells. Each midpoint is decoded into one matrix access in constant time, yielding O(log(r*c+1)) probes. Decoding uses only scalar indices; it does not allocate a flattened grid.
“O(log(r*c + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The cross-row ordering makes the virtual row-major array sorted.
“O(log(r*c + 1)) time, O(r*c + 1) auxiliary space”: Virtual row-major access uses division and remainder directly, so an r*c copied flat array is unnecessary.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Larger matrices can require logarithmically many midpoint probes to verify presence or absence.
